OSPS-AC-01.01.justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and accepts only secure methods, not SMS. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882

OSPS-AC-02.01.justification: A new member gets read access, the organization's base permission (gh api orgs/btclib-org --jq .default_repository_permission). Every higher grant is assigned by hand, through an issue in btclib-org/.github that an owner other than the one asking approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made

OSPS-AC-03.01.justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires a pull request for every change to main. Its one bypass actor, the maintainer, is in pull_request mode, which excuses the rule only while merging a pull request and permits no direct push. Issue 4 removes that bypass. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/issues/4 https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-AC-03.02.justification: The main-integrity ruleset forbids deleting main and has no bypass actor. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-AC-04.01.justification: The default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only at the organization and the repository, and cannot approve pull requests. Every workflow also sets permissions: contents: read at the top. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning

OSPS-AC-04.02.justification: Every workflow sets permissions: contents: read at the top, and a job adds a write scope only where it uses it. zizmor's excessive-permissions audit runs in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#what-every-workflow-does

OSPS-BR-01.01.justification: No workflow uses pull_request_target or workflow_run. Event fields and inputs reach run: steps only through env:, and zizmor's template-injection audit in the required lint check refuses the unsafe form. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml

OSPS-BR-01.03.justification: Pull-request runs use the pull_request and pull_request_review_comment triggers, which give a fork no secrets and a read-only token. The review job, which holds a secret, runs only when the head repository is this one. The mention job holds a secret on any pull request's issue comment, and there checks out the default branch. It answers only a comment whose author is an owner, a member or a collaborator, and its tools exclude Bash, edits, writes, file reads and every tool that runs code. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-claude-review.yml

OSPS-BR-01.04.justification: A workflow_dispatch input is either mutation.yml's profile, a choice from a fixed list, or verified-signatures.yml's before and after, which the called workflow reads through env: and refuses unless they are commit shas. A release tag's name is checked against the package version before anything is built. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/mutation.yml

OSPS-BR-02.01.justification: Each release has a unique calendar version (YYYY.M.D), set by a signed v* tag. release.yml refuses a tag that disagrees with the package version or is not on main, and PyPI never accepts a version twice. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/releases

OSPS-BR-02.02.justification: Every release asset carries the version in its file name: the sdist, the wheel, the CycloneDX SBOM (base58_bech32-2026.10.23.cdx.json) and the attestation bundle (v2026.10.23.intoto.jsonl). The attestation binds each asset to its digest. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/releases/latest

OSPS-BR-03.01.justification: Every official channel the project lists is served over HTTPS only: the GitHub repository, its issue tracker and advisories, and the documentation at https://base58-bech32.readthedocs.io/.

OSPS-BR-03.02.justification: Releases are distributed through PyPI and GitHub Releases, both HTTPS only. PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations and the GitHub release a Sigstore bundle. https://pypi.org/project/base58-bech32/

OSPS-BR-04.01.justification: The GitHub release body is RELEASE_NOTES.md's entry: what a user must act on, breaking and security changes included. CHANGELOG.md lists every change. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

OSPS-BR-05.01.justification: Python dependencies come from PyPI, and the required test check runs the suite with uv from the committed uv.lock with --locked. pre-commit installs its hooks at the revisions .pre-commit-config.yaml names. Third-party actions are pinned by commit SHA. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#uvlock

OSPS-BR-06.01.justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing. The GitHub release carries a Sigstore build-provenance bundle over each asset's SHA-256. The tag is signed. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/releases/latest

OSPS-BR-07.01.justification: Secret scanning and push protection are on, so a push carrying a recognised credential is refused. The detect-private-key and detect-secrets hooks run in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.secrets.baseline

OSPS-BR-07.02.justification: A secret is an environment secret that only the owners reach. A secret kept in any other store is recorded in the REPOSITORY.md of the repository that uses it, and btclib-org/.github's tests/secrets_test.py refuses an unrecorded one. A secret is rotated when an owner changes or an exposure is suspected. The secrets kept outside an environment are rotated before they are a year old, and the list is reviewed yearly. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning

OSPS-DO-01.01.justification: The user documentation is README.md, whose Python example tests/readme_test.py runs, and the API reference and migration page on Read the Docs. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/README.md#an-address-of-each-format https://base58-bech32.readthedocs.io/

OSPS-DO-02.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md says where a defect is filed, and the bug-report form asks for what a report needs. SECURITY.md sends a vulnerability to a private channel instead. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml

OSPS-DO-03.01.justification: SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command for the release assets, and RELEASING.md the check that rebuilds the sdist from its tag. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-03.02.justification: The verify command pins the signer: --repo names this repository, --signer-workflow the organization's reusable-build.yml and --source-ref the release tag. It passed on the v2026.10.23 wheel. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-04.01.justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*: only the latest release is supported, a fix ships as a new release, and nothing is backported. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-05.01.justification: SECURITY.md: only the latest release is supported, so a release stops receiving security updates when the next one is published. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-06.01.justification: The package has no runtime dependency: pyproject.toml declares dependencies = []. uv obtains the development dependencies from PyPI and pins them in uv.lock, and Dependabot tracks them weekly with a seven-day cooldown. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#dependabot-and-pre-commitci

OSPS-DO-07.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md gives the build: uv is the only prerequisite, uv sync builds the environment from uv.lock, and uv build produces the sdist and wheel. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-01.01.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's Roles names who holds access to sensitive resources. fametrano is the maintainer. Every owner, named there by login, is an administrator of every repository and a reviewer of the publishing environments. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-GV-01.02.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's *Roles* describes the maintainer, owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-GV-02.01.justification: Proposed changes and usage obstacles are discussed publicly in the repository's GitHub issues (with a question form) and pull requests; cross-repository questions go to btclib-org/.github's tracker. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/issues

OSPS-GV-03.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: one subject per pull request, the local gates, the review and the landing. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-03.02.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what a contribution must meet: one subject, a Signed-off-by trailer on every commit, the gates CI runs, 100% line and branch coverage, and a review against REVIEWING.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-04.01.justification: A grant of write or admin, to any repository of the organization, is an issue in btclib-org/.github that states the reason, and an owner other than the one asking approves it there. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made

OSPS-LE-01.01.justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer, Dependabot's and pre-commit.ci's aside. Web commits are signed off automatically. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py

OSPS-LE-02.01.justification: The source code is under the MIT license, which the OSI approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-LE-02.02.justification: The released wheels and sdist declare License-Expression: MIT, the same OSI-approved license as the source. https://pypi.org/project/base58-bech32/

OSPS-LE-03.01.justification: The license text is the repository's root LICENSE file. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-LE-03.02.justification: The LICENSE file ships inside every release asset: the sdist root and the wheel's .dist-info/licenses/. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-QA-01.01.justification: The repository is public on GitHub at a static URL. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32

OSPS-QA-01.02.justification: Git history on GitHub records every change with its author, committer, date and signature; linear history and no force-pushes on main keep that record from being rewritten. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/commits/main

OSPS-QA-02.01.justification: pyproject.toml declares the direct dependencies, none at run time and the development tools in dependency groups, and the committed uv.lock pins them. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml

OSPS-QA-02.02.justification: The release is pure Python. Every GitHub release attaches a CycloneDX SBOM, generated from the built wheel and covered by the release attestation. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/releases/latest

OSPS-QA-03.01.justification: main requires the listed status checks. enforce_admins is off, so an admin merge without them is a manual bypass, which the control allows. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-QA-04.01.justification: The organization standard's section 2 (*Which repositories, and how far*) lists every repository of btclib-org and its tier, and the organization profile lists the published packages. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#which-repositories-and-how-far

OSPS-QA-04.02.justification: The project has no additional subproject repository: each release is built from this one repository, and the package has no runtime dependency. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml

OSPS-QA-05.01.justification: No generated executable is committed. The only file git treats as binary is the Sphinx inventory docs/source/_inventories/python.inv, and fuzz/corpus/ holds input seeds for the fuzzers.

OSPS-QA-05.02.justification: No executable, library or compiled file is committed. The Sphinx inventory docs/source/_inventories/python.inv and the fuzz seeds under fuzz/corpus/ are data, and .clusterfuzzlite/build.sh is the only file with the executable bit, a shell script.

OSPS-QA-06.01.justification: test.yml's aggregate check ('test: every job passed') runs the test suite on every pull request and is a required status check on main. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

OSPS-QA-06.02.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the command that runs the suite. Its *What gates a merge, and what only reports* lists the workflows that run it on every pull request, on main and on a schedule, and which of them gate a merge. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-QA-06.03.justification: The policy is 100% line and branch coverage (CONTRIBUTING.md, standard section 8). pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100, so untested new code fails the required test check. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml

OSPS-QA-07.01.justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires one approving review from somebody other than the author, but it carries a temporary bypass for the maintainer, and pull requests 3 and 5 merged through it with no approving review. Issue 4 removes the bypass after the first release. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/issues/4 https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-SA-01.01.justification: ARCHITECTURE.md gives the modules, their layers bottom-up and what each may import, which tests/imports_test.py holds. ASSURANCE_CASE.md's Threat model and Trust boundaries name the actors, the caller and the adversary, and what each can do. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#trust-boundaries

OSPS-SA-02.01.justification: The API reference at https://base58-bech32.readthedocs.io/ is generated from the docstrings of every public module, and tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module is missing from it. CONTRIBUTING.md's The public surface states what is public.

OSPS-SA-03.01.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md is the security assessment: what is claimed, the threat model, the trust boundaries and how each common implementation weakness is countered; SECURITY.md's limitations section records the known residual risks. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

OSPS-SA-03.02.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Threat model* names what is defended, the adversaries and what is not defended, and *Trust boundaries* maps the attack surface where untrusted input enters, each argument naming the file, test or workflow behind it. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

OSPS-VM-01.01.justification: SECURITY.md's *Reporting a vulnerability* gives the private channels, a GitHub security advisory or email, and the timeframes: a report is acknowledged within 7 days, and a fix or a published advisory follows within 90 days. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability

OSPS-VM-02.01.justification: SECURITY.md names the security contacts: a private GitHub security advisory, or email to security at btclib dot org. GOVERNANCE.md's Roles says that address reaches every organization owner. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-VM-03.01.justification: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled, and SECURITY.md points to it (the Security tab's 'Report a vulnerability') and gives an email address as the alternative. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/security/advisories/new

OSPS-VM-04.01.justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories on this repository, each naming the release that fixes it. None has been published yet. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/security/advisories

OSPS-VM-04.02.justification: The CycloneDX SBOM a release attaches lists, in its vulnerabilities array, every vulnerability that the tree's .github/vex.toml judges not to affect the release, with the reason. A tree with no such judgement has no vex.toml, and its SBOM has no vulnerabilities key. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing

OSPS-VM-05.01.justification: The standard sets the threshold: actions/dependency-review-action fails a pull request that adds or changes a dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or with a licence outside the allow-list. Its settings are one file, btclib-org/.github's .github/dependency-review.yml. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/dependency-review.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning

OSPS-VM-05.02.justification: release.yml runs uv audit over every dependency the wheel declares, none today, and every publish job needs it to succeed. An advisory, or a service it cannot reach, stops the release. The only exemption is an id that the tree's own .github/vex.toml, carried into the release's signed SBOM, states as not affecting it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing

OSPS-VM-05.03.justification: The required lint check audits the whole uv.lock, every dependency group, on every pull request: check_audit.py --all-groups runs uv audit, which reads OSV's malicious-package (MAL-) entries as well as advisories. Any such entry fails the check, and so does an OSV that cannot be reached. The audit's only exemption is a .github/vex.toml entry, reviewed like any other change. The required Dependency review check also blocks a change that adds a dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or a licence outside the allow-list. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning

OSPS-VM-06.01.justification: The standard's section 5 sets a threshold of zero for ruff: select = ALL, bandit's S rules included, and each finding is fixed or suppressed in place with a reason. zizmor holds workflows to the same, in the required lint check. CodeQL runs on every pull request, but the standard sets no threshold for its alerts. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#5-ruff

OSPS-VM-06.02.justification: The required lint check runs .pre-commit-config.yaml on every pull request (ruff with the S rules, strict mypy, zizmor, detect-secrets) and blocks the merge on any finding not suppressed in place with a reason. CodeQL also runs on every pull request but is not a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/lint.yml

access_continuity.justification: The organization has three owners, fametrano, giacomocaironi and pmazzocchi, each an administrator of this repository and a reviewer of its publishing environments. If one becomes unavailable, the other two can still close issues, merge changes and release. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity

accessibility_best_practices.justification: The package is a library of functions with no user interface: no terminal prompt, no GUI and no web front end, and nothing under src/ calls input or print. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32

assurance_case.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md gives the threat model (what is defended, the adversaries, what is not defended), the trust boundaries, the secure design principles and the common implementation weaknesses with what counters each, naming the file, test or workflow behind every argument. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

automated_integration_testing.justification: test.yml runs the test suite on every pull request and on every push to main that changes more than Markdown, and its aggregate job `test: every job passed` is a required check. The os-ubuntu, os-macos and os-windows workflows run it on every supported interpreter weekly and before a release. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

build.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md gives the build: uv is the only prerequisite, uv sync builds the environment from uv.lock and uv build produces the sdist and wheel. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32?tab=contributing-ov-file

build_common_tools.justification: The build uses uv with the uv_build backend, the standard tools of a Python package. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32?tab=contributing-ov-file

build_floss_tools.justification: uv, uv_build, and every tool CONTRIBUTING.md names are FLOSS. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32?tab=contributing-ov-file

build_non_recursive.justification: This tree builds no native binaries, so there is no recursive-build question to answer. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml

build_preserve_debug.justification: No native build or installation step exists to strip or preserve debugging information. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml

build_repeatable.justification: Rebuilt from the tag v2026.10.23 with the uv named in the wheel, the sdist and the wheel are byte-identical to the released files (SHA-256 compared on 2026-10-23). Every week sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds the latest release's sdist from its tag and passes only if it matches the release's attested digest; it has run by hand, and its first scheduled run is Sunday 2026-10-25. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml

build_reproducible.justification: The sdist is built with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the commit and normalized by .github/scripts/normalize_sdist.py. A rebuild of v2026.10.23 gave the same SHA-256 as the released sdist and wheel, and RELEASING.md's Rebuild a release from its tag gives the command. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/RELEASING.md#rebuild-a-release-from-its-tag

build_standard_variables.justification: This tree builds no native binaries -- it is pure Python on the uv_build backend -- so there is no compiler or linker invocation for CC/CFLAGS/LDFLAGS to reach. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml

bus_factor.justification: fametrano wrote almost all of the code and is the only person who knows it in depth. This repository opened on 2026-10-17 with the Base58 and bech32 code moved from btclib and new SS58 and CashAddr codecs. Since 2026-10-17, 16 of the 31 commits are fametrano's and 10 are pmazzocchi's, an organization owner, whose changes fametrano approved; 3 are Dependabot's, 1 is pre-commit.ci's and 1 is an outside contributor's. git log --follow at btclib 8e87317b4 shows fametrano made 109 of 111 commits to base58.py and 62 of 64 to bech32.py. The claude account in the contributors graph comes from Co-Authored-By trailers on AI-assisted commits. giacomocaironi, also an organization owner, has made no commit here. The organization owners administer every repository. Knowledge of the code rests on fametrano alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/graphs/contributors

code_of_conduct.justification: btclib-org/.github's CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md is this repository's code of conduct, through GitHub's organization-wide default; the community-profile API reports it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

code_review_standards.justification: REVIEWING.md states what a review checks, how a finding is written and what clears a pull request; the part shared by every repository is followed by what this tree checks in particular. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/REVIEWING.md

coding_standards.justification: pyproject.toml selects every ruff rule (select = ["ALL"]) with a documented ignore list, and runs mypy in strict mode. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml

coding_standards_enforced.justification: ruff-check, ruff-format and mypy run as pre-commit hooks, and lint.yml runs the same .pre-commit-config.yaml in CI as a required check, so the style is enforced automatically rather than by review alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml

contribution_requirements.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the public-surface, input-validation, lint-gate and 100%-coverage requirements a contribution must meet before it can land. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

contributors_unassociated.justification: fametrano is the only significant contributor. pmazzocchi, an organization owner, has made 10 commits; pmazzocchi and fametrano are associated: both are CheckSig co-founders, as their GitHub profiles state. One outside contributor, harshith7002, has made one commit (pull request 45, convertbits' width limit). giacomocaironi, also an organization owner, has made no commit here. https://github.com/fametrano https://github.com/pmazzocchi

copyright_per_file.justification: Every Python file opens with "Copyright (c) The btclib developers", and ruff's flake8-copyright rule (CPY001) keeps it there, e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/src/base58_bech32/__init__.py

crypto_algorithm_agility.justification: The two hashes are fixed by the formats: Base58Check's checksum is double SHA-256 and SS58's is BLAKE2b-512, so a user cannot switch to another without leaving the format. They detect typing errors and authenticate nothing. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/README.md

crypto_call.justification: The only primitives are hashlib's sha256 (Base58Check) and blake2b (SS58), called from the standard library and not reimplemented. What the package writes itself is what the specifications define above them: the bech32 and CashAddr checksums, which are BCH error-detecting codes and not cryptography. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32

crypto_certificate_verification.justification: base58-bech32 performs no network communications, so it uses no TLS: no module under src/ imports socket, ssl, http or urllib. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32

crypto_credential_agility.justification: base58-bech32 is a library with no configuration file, credential store or password: it encodes and decodes the bytes and strings a caller passes in, and keeps nothing. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

crypto_floss.justification: no closed source dependencies: the standard library alone

crypto_keylength.justification: The package generates and uses no cryptographic key. A key or WIF a caller passes is a payload to encode, and SHA-256 and BLAKE2b take no key. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32

crypto_password_storage.justification: The package stores no password and authenticates no one: it has no user, account or secret of its own.

crypto_pfs.justification: The package implements no network key-agreement protocol: it performs no network communications at all.

crypto_published.justification: Every algorithm is a published one: SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) in Base58Check's double-hash checksum and BLAKE2b (RFC 7693) in SS58's. bech32, bech32m and CashAddr use the BCH codes their specifications publish, which detect errors and are not cryptography. Each format is checked against the vectors its authors publish. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/README.md

crypto_random.justification: The package draws no random number: nothing under src/ imports random or secrets or reads os.urandom. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32

crypto_tls12.justification: base58-bech32 performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32

crypto_used_network.justification: base58-bech32 does not use the network: no module under src/ imports socket, ssl, http or urllib. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32

crypto_verification_private.justification: base58-bech32 performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32

crypto_weaknesses.justification: No SHA-1 or MD5 appears under src/: hashlib is called for sha256 (Base58Check, in base58.py) and blake2b (SS58, in ss58.py) alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32

dco.justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a pull request with a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer. Dependabot's and pre-commit.ci's commits are exempt. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py

delivery_mitm.justification: Distribution channels use HTTPS exclusively: GitHub, and PyPI through Trusted Publishing. [osps_br_03_02]

delivery_unsigned.justification: Releases are published to PyPI and GitHub Releases and installed with pip from PyPI, all over HTTPS. No package or hash is fetched over plain HTTP. https://pypi.org/project/base58-bech32/ https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/releases

dependency_monitoring.justification: Dependabot version updates cover uv, github-actions and docker, and Dependabot security updates are on. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml

description_good.justification: base58-bech32 implements the binary-to-text codecs of cryptocurrency addresses and keys, Base58, Base58Check, bech32, bech32m, SS58 and CashAddr, in typed Python with no runtime dependency. https://base58-bech32.readthedocs.io/

discussion.justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.

documentation_achievements.justification: README.md links the OpenSSF Scorecard, Best Practices and Baseline badges on the lines the organization standard reserves for them. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/README.md

documentation_architecture.justification: ARCHITECTURE.md gives the modules bottom-up and what each may import, read from the import statements in src/. tests/imports_test.py holds the rule: it checks every file's imports against that table and refuses a module that reaches sideways or up, a bare import of the root included. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md

documentation_basics.justification: README.md says what the package holds and what it does not, how to install it, and gives a first use that tests/readme_test.py runs; CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md and ASSURANCE_CASE.md cover the rest. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/README.md

documentation_current.justification: The docs build is gated in CI as a required check (docs.yml, `-n -W`), tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module has no API page, and tests/readme_test.py runs every Python block of README.md, so neither the reference generated from the docstrings nor the README's example can drift from the code. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/docs.yml

documentation_interface.justification: Every public module and function carries a docstring, gated by ruff's pydocstyle rules and pydoclint, and docs/source's automodule pages render them into the API reference published at https://base58-bech32.readthedocs.io/; tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module is missing from them.

documentation_quick_start.justification: README.md's *An address of each format* is a first use: a WIF in Base58Check, a bech32 address decoded to its witness program, an SS58 address re-encoded for another chain, and a CashAddr address decoded. tests/readme_test.py runs it, so it is the one the suite checks. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/README.md#an-address-of-each-format

documentation_roadmap.justification: ROADMAP.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, is reviewed every September and states what is maintained, what is intended and what is deliberately not. This repository's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/ROADMAP.md

documentation_security.justification: SECURITY.md's Limitations, not vulnerabilities states the known limits: secret material is not zeroized and nothing is constant-time. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/SECURITY.md#limitations-not-vulnerabilities

dynamic_analysis.justification: Every release runs the test suite before it is published: release.yml calls test.yml, and the PyPI upload runs only if it passes. The suite fails below 100% coverage, branches included. ClusterFuzzLite fuzzing ran by hand on 2026-10-18 and on schedule on 2026-10-20 and passes, and it and cosmic-ray mutation testing are scheduled weekly. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml

dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions.justification: pytest, the mutation runs and the ClusterFuzzLite targets run Python without -O, so every assert is checked. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml

dynamic_analysis_fixed.justification: No fuzzing or mutation-testing finding is open. The scheduled fuzz run of 2026-10-20 and the scheduled mutation run of 2026-10-19 passed. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/actions/workflows/fuzz.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/actions/workflows/mutation.yml

dynamic_analysis_unsafe.justification: This tree ships pure Python, a memory-safe language; it produces no software written in a memory-unsafe language for a dynamic memory-safety tool to run against. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml

enhancement_responses.justification: Every enhancement request filed since the repository opened on 2026-10-17, such as issues 19 to 25, is the maintainer's own, and all are closed. Nobody else has filed one, so none is unanswered. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/issues

external_dependencies.justification: pyproject.toml declares `dependencies = []` -- the package imports the standard library alone, which tests/imports_test.py asserts of every module -- and the test and tooling dependencies in its dependency-groups, resolved and pinned in the committed uv.lock. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml

floss_license.justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).

floss_license_osi.justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).

governance.justification: GOVERNANCE.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, documents the decision model and every role a contributor, reviewer or owner holds; this tree's README.md links it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md

hardened_site.justification: The project page https://btclib.org/base58-bech32/ sends Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self', frame-ancestors 'none'), Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options DENY and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff (curl -sI, 2026-10-23). The repository on github.com sends all four. PyPI's project page sends the last three and no CSP; that is PyPI's to set.

hardening.justification: ruff's select = ["ALL"] includes the bandit S rules, so a hardening defect such as unsafe deserialization or shell injection fails the lint gate. CodeQL also runs on every pull request and every push to main. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml

implement_secure_design.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Secure design principles* applies Saltzer and Schroeder's principles one by one -- economy of mechanism, fail-safe defaults, complete mediation, open design, least privilege, psychological acceptability -- each to the file or test that carries it. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

input_validation.justification: Every public function validates its inputs and refuses what is invalid with a Base58Bech32TypeError or Base58Bech32ValueError, as CONTRIBUTING.md's *The public surface* requires. tests/input_validation_test.py drives the rule over every public function, and tests/fuzz_test.py holds every decoder to it on hostile strings. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

installation_common.justification: `python -m pip install --upgrade base58-bech32` installs it from PyPI, as README.md says, and pypi-install.yml installs the published version on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows after each release and weekly. https://pypi.org/project/base58-bech32/

installation_development_quick.justification: `uv sync` installs the whole development environment in one command, uv being the only tool to install first; CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* section gives it beside `uv run pytest` and the lint gate. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

installation_standard_variables.justification: Installation is `pip install`, which follows pip's and the interpreter's own install-location conventions; there is no project-specific installer that could diverge from that convention. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml

interfaces_current.justification: ruff's UP and FA rules flag deprecated constructs, and pytest turns every warning into an error. deps-latest and deps-oldest run the suite weekly at the newest and the floor versions. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml

internationalization.justification: The package produces no text for end users and sorts none: it converts bytes to ASCII strings and back, and its exceptions are English messages for developers. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32

know_common_errors.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md lists the common implementation weaknesses that apply here, among them CWE-20 (input validation), CWE-209 (sensitive information in errors) and CWE-400 (resource consumption), and what counters each. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#common-implementation-weaknesses

know_secure_design.justification: The primary developer maintains ASSURANCE_CASE.md, whose *Secure design principles* section applies Saltzer and Schroeder's principles to the code one by one. No security review of it has been done yet. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#secure-design-principles

license_location.justification: Non-trivial license location file in repository: <https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/LICENSE>.

license_per_file.justification: Every Python file states "Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying LICENSE file or https://opensource.org/license/mit", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/src/base58_bech32/__init__.py

maintained.justification: The first release, v2026.10.18, was published on 2026-10-18, a day after the repository opened. The second, v2026.10.23, followed on 2026-10-23, after 22 pull requests merged between the two. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/releases

maintenance_or_update.justification: Only the latest release is supported and nothing is backported (SECURITY.md). release.yml compares each release's public API with the previous tag's using griffe; v2026.10.23 is the first release with a previous tag, and RELEASE_NOTES.md lists what a user must act on to upgrade, four breaking changes in v2026.10.23. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

no_leaked_credentials.justification: detect-secrets baseline gated by pre-commit, and GitHub secret scanning with push protection enabled on the repository: https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.secrets.baseline

regression_tests_added50.justification: Bug fixes merged since 2026-10-17 each add a test: pull request 45 (convertbits width, closes 38) changes tests/bech32_test.py, 39 (closes 37) is a test fix, and 33 (b58decode_check, closes 28) changes eight test files. REVIEWING.md asks of every change whether what it adds is tested, and the 100% line and branch coverage gate fails a fix whose new code no test runs. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/REVIEWING.md https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates

release_notes.justification: RELEASE_NOTES.md holds each release's notes, and release.yml publishes the tag's section as the GitHub release body. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/releases/tag/v2026.10.18

release_notes_vulns.justification: v2026.10.23 fixes no published vulnerability and no advisory exists. It fixes three issues the maintainer labelled security: the missing length limits of bech32 and b58decode (issues 8 and 9) and the checksum quoted by b58decode_check (issue 28), and RELEASE_NOTES.md names the limit and the quoting. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/releases/tag/v2026.10.23

repo_distributed.justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git is distributed.

repo_interim.justification: development is on the main branch of https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32

repo_public.justification: Repository on GitHub, which provides public git repositories with URLs.

repo_track.justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git can track the changes, who made them, and when they were made.

report_process.justification: Bugs are reported on the GitHub issue tracker, through the issue forms under .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/, as CONTRIBUTING.md's *The issue tracker* describes: <https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/issues>. Vulnerabilities go through SECURITY.md instead: <https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/SECURITY.md>.

report_responses.justification: Five bug reports have been filed since the repository opened on 2026-10-17, issues 37, 38, 40, 41 and 42, all by pmazzocchi on 2026-10-19. Each got a comment or a linked change within the day and all are closed by 2026-10-21. Issues 54 and 57 are the maintainer's own tasks. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/issues

report_tracker.justification: Each repository uses its own GitHub Issues tracker for individual issues, with issue forms under .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/, and an organization-wide tracker in btclib-org/.github for cross-repository findings. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/issues

require_2FA.justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member. https://github.com/btclib-org

roles_responsibilities.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's Roles names the maintainer, the owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

secure_2FA.justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication and allows only secure methods: TOTP apps, security keys or passkeys, and GitHub Mobile, not SMS. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882

security_review.justification: No security review of this repository has been done. SECURITY.md's *Security review* says so, and ASSURANCE_CASE.md is what one will be done against. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-review

signed_releases.justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing, and each GitHub release a Sigstore provenance bundle. SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/releases/latest

sites_password_security.justification: Project sites are GitHub, PyPI and Read the Docs; this repository runs no site of its own that stores user passwords -- authentication is GitHub's and PyPI's, not this project's. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/SECURITY.md

small_tasks.justification: The label good first issue marks a small task for a first contribution, as CONTRIBUTING.md says, and one search lists the open ones across the organization. Issue 38 carried it and an outside contributor fixed it; no open issue in this repository carries it now. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-issue-tracker https://github.com/search?q=org%3Abtclib-org+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22+is%3Aopen&type=issues

static_analysis.justification: mypy in strict mode, ruff with every rule and CodeQL's python analysis.

static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities.justification: CodeQL's python analysis (codeql.yml) runs on a schedule, on every pull request and on every push to main, and ruff's `select = ["ALL"]` includes the bandit-derived S rules, both FLOSS static-analysis tools looking for common vulnerabilities. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml

static_analysis_fixed.justification: No static-analysis finding is open: CodeQL has no open alert, and ruff and mypy findings fail the required lint check. The 29 open code-scanning alerts are OpenSSF Scorecard's scores for pinning (26), code review, maintenance and branch protection. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml

static_analysis_often.justification: On every pull request and every push to main: https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/actions/workflows/lint.yml, https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/actions/workflows/codeql.yml

test.justification: test.yml runs the suite, gated at 100% line and branch coverage, against vectors their authors publish: Bitcoin Core's and the base58 package's for Base58, BIP173's and BIP350's for bech32, Substrate's and polkadot-js' for SS58, and the CashAddr specification's. tests/_data/README.md pins each vendored file to its upstream commit. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

test_branch_coverage80.justification: pyproject.toml sets branch = true under [tool.coverage.run], and the 100% fail_under gate includes branches: https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml

test_continuous_integration.justification: test.yml runs the suite on every pull request and on every push to main that changes more than Markdown files. Its aggregate job, test: every job passed, is a required check on main. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

test_policy.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md makes 100% coverage a gate every change must pass, so new functionality comes with its tests. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates

test_policy_mandated.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires 100% line and branch coverage, and fail_under = 100.0 fails the CI gate on any new code without a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

test_statement_coverage80.justification: pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100.0, gated on every pull request by test.yml. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml

test_statement_coverage90.justification: pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100.0 under [tool.coverage.report], and the required test check enforces it on every pull request: https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml

tests_are_added.justification: The required check test: every job passed fails any pull request that leaves a line or branch untested, so a change to src/ cannot land without its tests. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged

tests_documented_added.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the 100% coverage gate, so new functionality is not accepted without a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

two_person_review.justification: v2026.10.23 shipped 5 of 22 pull requests approved by somebody other than the author and other than fametrano. main's ruleset requires one approving review from somebody other than the author. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

updateable_reused_components.justification: At runtime the package reuses only the standard library. The test and tooling components are PyPI packages pinned in uv.lock and bumped by Dependabot, and the deps-latest sentinel runs the full suite against the upgraded set every week. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/deps-latest.yml

version_semver.justification: CalVer, YYYY.M.D, declared in pyproject.toml and explained in RELEASE_NOTES.md: the number says when a release was cut and promises nothing about compatibility, so a breaking change is announced in RELEASE_NOTES.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

version_tags.justification: Each release is tagged v<version> on the release commit, as RELEASING.md requires. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tags

version_tags_signed.justification: Every release tag is signed, and RELEASING.md reads each signature back. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tags

version_unique.justification: Each release carries a unique calendar version, YYYY.M.D, declared once in pyproject.toml and tagged v<version>. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/releases

vulnerabilities_critical_fixed.justification: No vulnerability is known and none is unfixed: the advisories list is empty and no Dependabot alert is open. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/security/advisories

vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days.justification: No vulnerability has been reported or published, and no Dependabot alert is open. Three issues labelled security, 8, 9 and 28, are hardening, not exploitable vulnerabilities, and v2026.10.23 fixes them. Each advisory would name the release that fixes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/security/advisories

vulnerability_report_credit.justification: No vulnerability has been reported to this repository, so there is no reporter to credit. SECURITY.md says how a report is made. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability

vulnerability_report_response.justification: No vulnerability report has been received since the repository opened on 2026-10-17. SECURITY.md promises an acknowledgement within 7 days. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/security/advisories

vulnerability_response_process.justification: SECURITY.md's Reporting a vulnerability gives the private channels (a GitHub security advisory, or security at btclib dot org), who can see a report, and how a CVE is requested. Private vulnerability reporting is enabled. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/SECURITY.md

warnings.justification: mypy strict with all relevant extra checks activated, see https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml

warnings_fixed.justification: Warnings are not tolerated: ruff, strict mypy and pytest's filterwarnings = ["error"] fail the required checks. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml

warnings_strict.justification: ruff runs with `select = ["ALL"]` (every rule family) and mypy runs with `strict = true`; both are zero-finding pre-commit hooks enforced again by the required lint workflow. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml
